claim: Automated AI-text detection is too unreliable to be a safe basis for action on application essays, and it is biased against the students with the most to lose. The peer-reviewed Stanford study (Liang et al., Patterns, 2023) ran 91 non-native-English TOEFL essays through 7 commercial GPT detectors and found ~61% were misflagged as AI-written, versus ~5% false-positive rate on native-English writing -- a bias rooted in non-native writers' lower lexical variability ('low perplexity'). Turnitin disabled or warned on its AI detector at major universities (e.g. Vanderbilt disabled it August 2023) over false-positive risk, and Turnitin's tool requires ~300+ words and can miss ~15% of AI text -- yet many supplemental essays are only 150-250 words, below the reliable threshold.

application.content: Do NOT treat any AI-detector score as ground truth for the student OR against them. For the student's protection: a genuinely human-written essay -- especially from a non-native English writer or a plain-style writer -- can be falsely flagged, so the defense is process evidence (drafts, version history, brainstorm notes) demonstrating authorship, not a low detector score. For Uplift's own pipeline: never gate or accuse based on a detector number; if 'sounds like AI' is a concern, redirect to the craft signal (concrete, irreplaceable voice per entry 007), which is both more reliable and more useful than a probabilistic detector. Counsel non-native English students to KEEP their drafts precisely because they are at 2-3x higher false-flag risk.

sources.citation: Liang, Yuksekgonul, Mao, Wu, Zou -- 'GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers,' Patterns 4(7):100779
sources.authorRole: Stanford University researchers, peer-reviewed (Cell Press / Patterns)

sources.citation: Turnitin admits there are some cases of higher false positives in AI writing detection tool | K-12 Dive
sources.authorRole: K-12 Dive (established education journalism) reporting Turnitin's own admission + Vanderbilt's disabling

connections.note: Because detectors are unreliable, AOs fall back on reading voice/specificity -- the craft signal in entry 007 is what actually drives human judgment.
Detector unreliability is one reason most schools (the 68% with no policy) have not built enforcement around detection.

provenanceTrail: Liang et al. is a peer-reviewed Patterns (Cell Press) article -- Tier-1 -- with the 61.3% vs 5.1% TOEFL/native false-positive figures and the low-perplexity mechanism quoted directly; corroborated across PubMed, PMC, ScienceDaily mirrors. Vanderbilt's Aug-2023 disabling of Turnitin's detector and Turnitin's own false-positive admission reported by K-12 Dive (Tier-2 established ed journalism); the ~750-wrongful-accusations-per-75,000-papers and 300-word-minimum / 15%-miss figures appeared across multiple 2023-2026 secondary sources but the load-bearing claims here rest on the peer-reviewed study + Turnitin's own admission. Marked semi-stable: bias direction is durable, but specific detector accuracy numbers and which tools admissions use will move.
